scenes.purpose: Introduce the topic of the President's election process.
scenes.teacher_script: Hello, young citizens! Today, we're going to explore how our country's highest office, the President of India, is chosen. It's a very unique and important process!

template_data.title: How is the President of India Elected?
template_data.subtitle: Understanding India's Unique Presidential Election

scenes.purpose: Explain that the President is elected indirectly by an Electoral College.
scenes.teacher_script: Unlike your local MLAs, the President is not directly elected by the common people. Instead, a special group of elected representatives form an 'Electoral College' to choose our President.

template_data.title: An Indirect Election by the Electoral College

attributes.name: Reason
attributes.value: To represent both the Union and the States fairly

scenes.purpose: Identify the key components of the Electoral College.
scenes.teacher_script: Let's see who are these important members that make up the Electoral College. They come from both our Parliament at the central level and our Legislative Assemblies in the states and Union Territories.

bullets: Elected Members of Lok Sabha (House of the People)
Elected Members of Rajya Sabha (Council of States)
Elected Members of State Legislative Assemblies (MLAs)
Elected Members of Legislative Assemblies of Delhi and Puducherry

scenes.purpose: Explain the concept of weighted votes for proportional representation.
scenes.teacher_script: Here's a fascinating twist! In the President's election, not all votes carry the same value. An MLA's vote value depends on the population of their state, ensuring proportional representation across the country.

attributes.name: MLAs' Vote Value
attributes.value: Calculated based on the population of their state

attributes.name: MPs' Vote Value
attributes.value: Equal for all MPs, calculated to balance state votes

attributes.name: Why Weighted?
attributes.value: To ensure states with larger populations have more say, and smaller states are also represented.

scenes.purpose: Describe the voting method: Proportional Representation by Single Transferable Vote and Secret Ballot.
scenes.teacher_script: The election uses a system called 'Proportional Representation by means of Single Transferable Vote.' Voters rank candidates in order of their preference, and the voting is done through a secret ballot.

template_data.title: How Votes are Cast and Counted

attributes.name: Ballot Type
attributes.value: Secret Ballot – ensuring free and fair election

scenes.purpose: Test the student's understanding of the Electoral College.
scenes.teacher_script: Great job learning about the Presidential election! Now, let's quickly test your memory. Which of these groups is part of the Electoral College?

template_data.question: Which of the following groups are members of the Electoral College that elects the President of India?
options: All citizens of India aged 18 and above
Elected members of Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies
Nominated members of Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies
Only the Chief Ministers of all states
template_data.explanation: The Electoral College comprises elected members of both Houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) and elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of all states, including Delhi and Puducherry.
